topic.readerProblem: A buyer deciding between Profound and Otterly.AI wants to know which AI visibility tracker fits their budget, team size and compliance needs, and what each one actually lists and costs.
topic.connection: Helps readers choose between a one-time AI visibility baseline (AEOeye) and a recurring tracker, and tells them honestly when Otterly.AI or Profound is the right category.

assessment: The page is documentation-based and says so near the top: it uses each vendor's own pricing pages, help-center articles and feature page as checked on 2026-10-03, with no hands-on testing. It gives a verdict first (Otterly.AI for a budgetable price, Profound for SOC 2/SSO/API/support and quote-based buying), a side-by-side table of only what the vendors publish, a note that Profound's Trial prompts cannot be customized, and the discrepancy between Profound's two engine lists. It does not claim anything about data accuracy, output quality or product experience, and it states Profound's brand price as not published rather than estimating one.

sources.supports: Lite $29 / Standard $189 / Premium $489 monthly with 15 / 100 / 400 prompts, the four base engines, Gemini / AI Mode / Claude add-on prices by plan, extra 100 prompts $99 on Standard and Premium and not available on Lite, API / MCP / Agent Analytics / Looker Studio connector on Standard and above, Enterprise from 1,000 prompts with Single Sign-On, annual billing 15% off, Agency Partner programme.
Otterly.AI offers a 7-day free trial with no credit card required and 50 search prompts.
Otterly collects data through public web interfaces because API data can differ from what users see, with Claude tracked through the API as the stated exception.

Brand plans are a free Trial (50 prompts daily for 7 days on ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, 1 language, 1 region, no history/exports/API/support) and a custom Enterprise plan (up to nine engines listed, all-time history, CSV/JSON, API, SSO/SAML + SOC 2, dedicated support, unlimited seats); Trial prompts cannot be customized; Agents and AI Marketer run on credits; no monthly brand price is listed.

Profound captures answers directly from the browser rather than APIs, runs every tracked prompt daily, and names its engines as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Google Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek (Grok where the pricing page lists Exa Search).
600 volunteers ran 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google's AI a combined 2,961 times; less than a 1 in 100 chance that ChatGPT or Google's AI gives the same brand list in any two responses.

checks: Writer (Sonnet): fetched Otterly's pricing page raw HTML with curl on 2026-10-03 and checked every plan price, prompt count, included engine, add-on price and Enterprise item against the page text; read the Otterly help-center pricing, trial and data-collection articles.

Writer (Sonnet): fetched Profound's pricing page raw HTML and checked the Trial and Enterprise rows, the nine-engine list, the 'cannot customize their prompts' FAQ and the absence of any brand price; compared its engine list with the Answer Engine Insights page and reported the Exa Search versus Grok difference as an item to confirm with the vendor.
Writer (Sonnet): confirmed the SparkToro study's design (600 volunteers, 12 prompts, 2,961 runs) and its under-1-in-100 identical-list finding against the page's raw text before citing it.

Writer (Sonnet): left out agency add-on prices and Profound's retired Starter/Growth figures because they were not in the server-rendered pricing HTML we could read; said only that the live page lists no brand price.

Writer (Sonnet): used first-hand AEOeye evidence only from the evidence pack and vendor study: the otterly.ai and tryprofound.com rows of the crawler access study (otterly.ai: no robots.txt, homepage and /llms.txt 403; tryprofound.com: no AI bots blocked or named, /llms.txt 404, no JSON-LD in served HTML) and AEOeye product facts (free 3-question ChatGPT audit, $29 one-time report, not a daily tracker).
